# the contributor audit: ordinary maximal-depth Brunn--Minkowski rigidity

Source: `candidate 6c56e9569b9982d7`.


none supplies a mixed-integer cap budget by itself.

## Section variation

At an interior candidate every through-point hyperplane is a proper
section. Except on its relative boundary, a section point is an interior
point of the body. The one-dimensional slice derivative under a normal
perturbation is therefore the asserted signed displacement, while it is
zero off the section. The displacement itself bounds the difference
quotient on the bounded projection. Fubini and dominated convergence
justify the angular derivative without smoothness. Its vanishing at a
directional minimum forces the section centroid to be the candidate.
The singleton-section convention covers dimension one.

## Active-cover and equality chain

If active normals at a deepest point did not positively balance, the
uniform own-inball slab gain and the gap on the complementary compact
set of normals would strictly increase every directional cap at a small
center displacement. Thus zero lies in their convex hull. A finite
positive balance covers the entire space by closed through-center caps,
even when those normals do not span the full dimension.

Under equality in the A-root Brunn--Minkowski inequality, the sum of the
two chosen deepest points is a deepest point in the Minkowski sum. Every
selected active normal forces equality at every step of the cap-volume
chain. Positive coefficients force each endpoint cap to have its own
ordinary minimum volume. Ordinary Brunn--Minkowski equality applies to
these positive full-dimensional convex caps and gives a common homothety
ratio.

The remaining translation alignment is essential and is proved: the
minimum face in that normal is exactly the proper cutting section, its
centroid is the endpoint deepest point, and the cap homothety maps those
faces. Hence every cap homothety has the same translation. Taking the
union over the covering active normals maps the entire first body onto
the second. This is not an inference from a single active cap. Conversely,
positive homothety gives the stated equality by volume scaling.

## Strict inclusion, uniqueness, and strict quasiconcavity

If a proper inclusion preserved A, sandwiching the midpoint Minkowski
body would force the equality case, whose ratio is one. Equal-volume
translated bodies cannot be in proper inclusion. This proves strict
monotonicity without assuming strict interior containment.

The direct quasiconcavity proof is also valid. For a putative equal-level
interior segment, an attaining intermediate cap either has different
endpoint thresholds, in which case strict slab monotonicity contradicts
the depth at one endpoint, or has a single common threshold. In the
latter case it is active at both endpoints and its section centroid would
have to equal two different points. Thus positive ordinary depth regions
below the maximum are full-dimensional strictly convex compact sets,
and the ordinary deepest point is unique.

The compatible-midpoint corollary follows by sandwiching with A-root
Brunn--Minkowski and using strict inclusion monotonicity. It gives exact
midpoint set equality and homothetic endpoints. Zero coefficients and
lower-dimensional bodies are expressly excluded from the rigidity claim.

The existing eight-base simplex example already satisfies this stronger
zero A-root equality on every selected forest edge. Its graph Helly
obstruction therefore remains valid. No new global Jensen or small-Helly
conclusion follows solely from the rigidity theorem.
